Hi Sarah / Tom —

Great to meet today — thanks for the time and for walking through the ACME use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Call recap (very high level)
- Primary use: in-product generation for analytics assistant (prompt->structured insights)
- Expected QPS: low-to-medium initially, scale to sustained throughput in Q1
- Data: mix of public + internal datasets; sensitive PII limited to hashed identifiers
- Decision criteria: latency (p95 < 600ms), cost per 1k tokens, and security controls (VPC/KMS)

Stakeholder mapping / asks from today
1) Economic buyer / final approver — who will sign the commercial terms? (You mentioned a finance sponsor)
2) Security & legal owner for initial security questionnaire and DPA (we’ll need SOC2 attestations and data flow details)
3) Procurement owner for contract routing and PO timelines

Immediate next steps
- Can you confirm the names/emails for the three owners above? (economic buyer, legal/security, procurement) — cc’ing Lauren from our side who will own contract routing.
- If you can share your NDA/standard procurement timeline, we’ll sequence ours to match. We typically do NDA -> MSA -> DPA; typical internal turn-times: NDA 2-3 business days, MSA 3-7 bd depending on redlines, DPA 3-5 bd.

Attachments: placeholder for ACME NDA we’ll use as starting point (please share yours if you prefer)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate on our side to get the initial NDA/MSA templates over and loop Legal once we have names.

Hi Sarah / Tom / Procurement team — looping in Rishi (Counsel) and David (Solutions) to propose how we’d like to sequence and who will own what on our side to keep the timeline tight.

Proposed routing & ownership (Redwood side):
- NDA: initial exchange — Marissa will send our NDA draft (attached); Procurement/ACME can counter. Redwood owner: Lauren (contracts intake). Target turnaround: 1-3 business days for standard NDA.
- MSA: start parallel drafting while NDA is in review if ACME is comfortable (helps compress timeline). Redwood owner: Rishi (legal) for redlines + comments. Target: 3-7 business days after initial redlines, but depends on scope.
- DPA: scope determined by data classification; can be appended as exhibit or separate. Redwood owner: Rishi with input from David (data flows). Target: 3-5 business days once scope locked.

Redline sequencing recommendation: NDA -> parallel MSA prep -> MSA redlines -> finalize DPA. If you prefer to review MSA only after NDA executed, we can hold off. Our experience shows parallel MSA prep shortens elapsed time.

What we need from ACME to hit the shorter timeline:
- Confirm whether ACME will provide a counter-NDA or prefers our template.
- If you want parallel MSA prep: provide any non-standard terms early (e.g., indemnity caps, data residency, auditors).
- SOC 2 report and security contact (Tom, if you can share a link or SOC2-ascertation email).

Attachments: Redwood MSA with our suggested redlines (Redwood-MSA-redlines_20260914.docx) — Rishi will review any ACME comments and consolidate.

Rishi — quick ask: if ACME pushes significant indemnity or data residency asks, can you give a 24-48h triage on material changes? That will help keep the timeline.

Thanks all — suggest a 15-min sync Wed morning (14 Sep) if that works; otherwise we’ll proceed async.

Best,
